subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should Codex computer `duration` accept only finite non-negative JSON numbers, preserve plain decimal-string compatibility, or continue allowing a broader JavaScript-coercible grammar?
rationale: The current docs and upstream protocol envelope do not settle the nested duration grammar, while the PR intentionally removes previously accepted inputs and only changes watchdog accounting; that compatibility contract needs an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Canonical numbers only
options.body: Reject every string duration at the computer-tool boundary and make execution and watchdog calculation consume the same finite non-negative numeric value.

options.title: Preserve decimal strings
options.body: Normalize plain decimal strings centrally and use the normalized value consistently in both the executor and outer deadline while rejecting hexadecimal, exponent, and fractional-string forms as explicitly chosen.

options.title: Land watchdog-only narrowing
options.body: Accept that execution and watchdog parsing may have different grammars and document the resulting compatibility and premature-timeout risk.

recommendation.title: Canonical numbers only
recommendation.body: Reject every string duration at the computer-tool boundary and make execution and watchdog calculation consume the same finite non-negative numeric value.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a compatibility decision for the bundled Codex computer integration rather than a mechanical test or formatting choice.
